facts.statement: payment has a single Deployment revision (created 06:45:29Z, change-cause null); no payment rollout occurred in the ~20 minutes before the alert.
payment's namespace events show no warnings or restarts in the window, and namespace-wide warnings do not involve payment or its dependencies.
The flag paymentFailure is ENABLED at variant 50%, the only enabled flag out of 18; it has no timestamp.
Payment logs the exception 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold' at warn level 31 times in 07:03-07:06Z, versus 19 'Transaction complete.' lines.
The error spans originate in payment's charge and PaymentService/Charge spans and propagate to checkout, frontend (422) and frontend-proxy.
payment's 5m server error ratio rose from 0.0998 at 07:04:08Z to 0.3716 at 07:06:08Z.
payment's failing Charge spans are fast (p95 about 4.17 ms vs 1.9 ms for successes), and the failures have no error spans on downstream calls (currency and product-catalog are clean).
Checkout's client-side Charge errors (0.0869/s) equal payment's server-side Charge errors; checkout logs show no errors.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check flagd config change history or git/ConfigMap history for paymentFailure, and confirm the enable timestamp matches the first error at 07:03:43Z.
hypotheses.statement: The paymentFailure flag was enabled at about 07:03Z, the start of the error onset.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Query checkout server spans and its dependency client spans around 06:47Z, and check its logs and events for that window.
hypotheses.statement: Checkout's p95 spike at 06:47:45Z (476 ms) is unrelated to payment and has a separate cause.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Change the flag in flagd, then watch service:sli_error_ratio:rate5m for payment and checkout drop back toward baseline.
hypotheses.statement: Disabling paymentFailure (or setting it to 0%) will return payment's error ratio to about 0.1% within the 5m window.

inferences.statement: payment is the origin of the incident. Checkout and the frontend are only reporting its failures, and no dependency is implicated.
The failures are the injected paymentFailure behavior, concentrated on gold-tier users, since all failures carry loyalty_level=gold and the 50% variant fits the ~40-60% failure share.

root_causes.cause: Injected or faulty failure path in payment's charge code: the paymentFailure flag (50%) is making charges fail with an 'Invalid token' error for gold-tier users, while the rest of the code path is fine. Disabling or reverting the flag should stop the errors.

The paymentFailure flag was switched on in flagd's configuration at 50%. The flag state has no change timestamp, so the enabling change is not identified; this is the config-side source of the trigger.

diagnosis.summary: payment is failing about 32% of Charge requests (onset about 07:03Z). Every failure is payment's own 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. loyalty_level=gold' error, thrown fast in charge code with no dependency errors. The one payment-related change is the paymentFailure flag, ENABLED at 50%, which is the likely injected fault. There was no payment rollout or pod change. Checkout, frontend and frontend-proxy only propagate the error. The flag's enable time is not recorded, so the link to onset is unconfirmed.

alternatives.why_not: payment has a single Deployment revision (ev_3ac470f34ba07c0e, created 06:45:29Z) with no rollout in the 20 minutes before the alert, so there is no bad release to revert.

No stuck or leaking process is indicated. Namespace events show no restarts or warnings for payment (ev_d1e42c3d05f3d4a9), and the failures are deliberate fast errors from the flag path, so a restart would leave the flag on and the errors would return.
The failures are fast, deterministic 'Invalid token' rejections for gold-tier users, not timeouts or saturation, so more replicas would not reduce the error ratio.

plan.no_action_reason: Root cause is the paymentFailure flag (ENABLED 50%) in flagd, which none of the available actions can change. Human action: set paymentFailure to OFF or 0% in flagd, then check payment's 5m error ratio falls to about 0.1%. The flag's enable time is still unconfirmed, so also find who enabled it.
plan.summary: payment fails about 32% of Charge requests because the paymentFailure flag is enabled at 50% in flagd. None of rollout_undo, restart_deployment or scale_deployment can change that, so I propose no action. A human should set paymentFailure to OFF (or 0%) in flagd and confirm payment's 5m error ratio returns to baseline.

facts.statement: The flagd flag paymentFailure is on with variant 50% and is the only enabled flag out of 18.

Payment's Charge handler rejects requests with 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold' (charge.js:48). It appears about 30 times between 07:03:02Z and 07:06:15Z, all at warn level.
Checkout's 20 recent error traces each run checkout PlaceOrder -> PaymentService/Charge -> payment Charge, and frontend returns HTTP 422 / gRPC 13 with the same payment message.
Payment's PaymentService/Charge server spans return STATUS_CODE_ERROR from 07:04Z while payment's p95 stays flat near 1.9 ms, so the failures are fast, not slow.
Checkout's 5m and 1m error ratios match payment's from 07:04Z onward, and checkout's client Charge spans start failing in the same minute.
Payment's downstream client spans show no new errors after 07:00Z. The only earlier error was a flagd EventStream blip around 06:58Z that cleared by about 07:00Z.
The payment and checkout deployments each have a single revision, created 06:45:29Z with no change-cause. product-catalog's single revision was created 06:45:31Z. None changed near 07:00Z.
Cluster warning events in the last 90 minutes are only readiness probe failures on otel-collector-agent, loki and otel-demo-alertmanager, all at or before 06:46Z. Payment has no warnings or restarts.
Payment has zero error-level log lines in the window, and checkout also has zero error-level lines.
frontend's PlaceOrder client errors and frontend-proxy egress errors rise from 07:04Z, peaking at about 0.08/s.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check the flagd flag config's change history or audit trail (ConfigMap/flagd source revisions) and the flagd logs for when paymentFailure changed from off to on.
hypotheses.statement: The paymentFailure flag was switched on at about 07:00-07:03Z through a flagd config change, which is the trigger.

hypotheses.statement: The failure only hits gold-tier users (the message names loyalty_level=gold), so the 50% rate may be a subset of users, not all charges.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Read payment's charge.js around line 48 to see which flag or condition throws this error, and confirm that the paymentFailure flag controls it.
hypotheses.statement: The error at charge.js:48 is a deliberate flag-driven injection in payment's code, not a bug.

inferences.statement: Checkout is a victim, not the cause: its only failing client span is Charge toward payment, its own self time is about 1 ms, and its failing spans show only the payment rejection.
The fault is inside payment. Its dependencies show no new errors and product-catalog, currency and email are clean, which rules out the shared product-catalog/kafka hypotheses.
Payment's failure is invisible to error-level log alerting, since it appears only as warn logs and error-status spans.

root_causes.cause: Payment's Charge handler returns errors for about half of requests, most likely because the paymentFailure flag (variant 50%, targeting off) is enabled. The flag's enable time is unconfirmed, but it is the only enabled flag and it matches the failure pattern. Payment fails fast, so this is not a latency or dependency problem.

Less likely: a payment-side code or config change not visible in rollout history (no payment revision after 06:45:29Z was found, and Prometheus returned no generation data). It cannot be ruled out until the flag and code path are checked.

diagnosis.summary: The checkout ErrorBudgetBurn is a downstream effect. Payment's Charge handler is rejecting about half of calls with 'Invalid token... loyalty_level=gold' (warn-level logs, fast failures), and checkout inherits this through PaymentService/Charge. The likely trigger is the paymentFailure flagd flag, which is on at 50% and is the only enabled flag. Its switch-on time is not yet confirmed. Neither payment nor checkout had a rollout near 07:00Z. Fix payment (flag or code path) first; checkout should recover once payment stops failing. Payment has no error-level logs, so error-log alerting would miss this.

alternatives.why_not: Payment and checkout each have a single revision created 06:45:29Z, long before the 07:00Z onset, so there is no bad release to roll back to. Undoing would not touch the flag.
Payment has no restarts or warnings and its failures are deliberate fast rejections, not a stuck or leaking process. A restart would not clear a flag-driven failure.
Payment's failures are fast (p95 flat near 1.9 ms) and not capacity-related, so more replicas would not reduce the 50% rejection rate.

plan.no_action_reason: Cause is the paymentFailure flagd flag, outside the allowed actions. A human should check flagd config to see who enabled it around 07:00-07:03Z and whether that was intended; if not, set it back to off. Then confirm the gold-tier scope and verify checkout recovers.
plan.summary: Checkout's burn is inherited from payment, whose Charge handler rejects about half of calls. The likely trigger is the paymentFailure flagd flag (on at 50%), which none of rollout_undo, restart_deployment or scale_deployment can change. No automated action is proposed; a human should turn the flag off or confirm it was intentionally enabled, then verify recovery.
